chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Let one of you apply perfume on the day of Friday, even if it is from a flask of his wife.'

key_terms.لِيَتَطَيَّبْ: Let him apply perfume / be perfumed

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on wearing perfume on Friday?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the Sunnah of *ittibāʿ* (following the Prophet) in personal grooming for Friday congregational prayers, reflecting the Shia emphasis on physical purity as an extension of spiritual readiness. The mention of the wife's flask highlights the domestic and accessible nature of this practice, encouraging believers to utilize available resources without extravagance. It serves as a practical reminder that respect for the communal gathering includes presenting oneself in a pleasant and clean manner.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Let each one of you apply perfume on the day of Friday, even if it is from a flask of his wife’.
en.sarwar: 13. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘On Friday you must apply perfume: even if it is from the perfumes of your wives.’”
